changes: WP-11-crash_recovery: complete crash recovery. Unified panic capture (banner + 16-GPR register snapshot + call traceback, serial AND red VGA; L1 panic-handler chain - a handler claiming recovery resumes the frame; OC_ASSERT). Core dumps persisted to /var/crash/core.dump (oc_dump_hdr_t + register block + kernel-stack window; serial hex fallback with no filesystem; dumpinfo decodes). 32-entry crashlog ring (vector/ring/err/rip/rsp/cr2/task/tid/pid + RTC) with crashlog + flush to /var/log/crash.log. HALT/REBOOT policy - the reboot path is the production 8042 + 0xCF9 reset, QEMU-verified panic -> reset -> second boot. Soft watchdog (1 s tick, boot-disarmed by documented decision; crashtest wd drives the real tick path). Kernel-stack overflow detection: guard page on every kthread stack, scheduler rsp bounds check, KERNEL STACK OVERFLOW attribution with the task name (crashtest ovf: burn -> guard #PF -> #DF -> attributed panic -> HALT). Ring-3 SIGSEGV: the delivery primitive shared with the syscall path; a faulting process with a handler gets a real signal (3-delivery ping-pong guard then force-kill, reset on exec); run sigsegv_test / stackovf / badapp. TUI crash containment: a ring-0 fault inside the TUI code window with an active guard longjmps back to the surviving desktop (Control Panel -> Crash test). New commands crashtest (panic/exc/pf/assert/wd/ovf/dump/policy) + dumpinfo; crashlog completed (224 -> 226); L1 interfaces 138 -> 146. Gates, on the release ISO: WP-11 E2E 14/14, regression 28/28, dhtest, cryptotest, SSH E2E 5/5, HTTPS E2E 7/7, BIOS + UEFI boots, 0 errors 0 warnings. The #DF boundary is stated in KNOWN_ISSUES 15.13. Build 240.
